title: How To Grow An Audience If You Have 0 Followers (It's Only 2 Habits)

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: I'm going to sound pretty arrogant for a second, but growing on social media is easy, and I actually mean that.
sentences.zh: 接下来这句话听起来会很狂，但在社交媒体上增长其实很简单，我是认真的。

sentences.en: I'm not just saying it because it's a good hook.
sentences.zh: 我不是因为它是个好钩子才这么说。

sentences.en: It is a good hook, but I never really had a problem growing on social media on any platform.
sentences.zh: 它确实是个好钩子，但我在任何平台上做社交媒体增长，从来就没遇到过什么问题。

sentences.en: So when I was outlining this video, I kind of asked myself, okay, why was it easy for me to grow?
sentences.zh: 所以当我给这期视频列大纲的时候，我问自己，好吧，为什么增长对我来说这么容易？

sentences.en: And it really came from me failing at like seven other different business models before I actually started on social media.
sentences.zh: 答案其实是，在我真正开始做社交媒体之前，我已经在其他七八种商业模式上失败过了。

sentences.en: So when I started on social media, I wasn't starting from scratch.
sentences.zh: 所以当我开始做社交媒体的时候，我并不是从零起步。

sentences.en: I had a bunch of high value skills under my belt.
sentences.zh: 我身上已经攒了一堆高价值技能。

sentences.en: Even though those prior businesses, thanks to Shiny Object Syndrome, failed and I tried so many different things, I tried digital art with like Photoshop.
sentences.zh: 尽管因为 Shiny Object Syndrome，之前的那些生意都失败了，我试了太多不同的东西，我试过用 Photoshop 做数字艺术。

sentences.en: I tried photography and charging for like in-person photo sessions.
sentences.zh: 我试过摄影，靠线下约拍收费。

sentences.en: I tried multiple agencies like Facebook ads, SEO, web design.
sentences.zh: 我试过好几家代理公司，做 Facebook 广告、SEO、网页设计。

sentences.en: I tried dropshipping twice.
sentences.zh: 我试过两次 dropshipping。

sentences.en: I tried building an e-commerce brand, like actually ordering this pretty much dropshipping twice.
sentences.zh: 我试过做一个电商品牌，说白了差不多就是又搞了两次 dropshipping。

sentences.en: And I probably even did a few more that I don't even register because they were so short lived.
sentences.zh: 可能还做过一些别的，我甚至都没印象了，因为太短命了。

sentences.en: It was like a week at a time.
sentences.zh: 每次就撑一周。

sentences.en: I'd start something and then I'd build the website.
sentences.zh: 我会开始一个项目，然后建好网站。

sentences.en: I'd get so excited about starting the LLC, and then the dopamine would fade and then I'd quit.
sentences.zh: 注册 LLC 的时候兴奋得不行，然后多巴胺一退，我就放弃了。

sentences.en: And that was kind of unfortunate because as a teenager, for some reason, it was just the bane of my existence to get a 9 to 5 job, right?
sentences.zh: 这其实挺惨的，因为作为一个青少年，不知道为什么，找一份朝九晚五的工作对我来说就是人生的噩梦，对吧？

sentences.en: I looked around me, I looked at my parents.
sentences.zh: 我看了看身边的人，看了看我父母。

sentences.en: I love my parents, but I looked at the older generation. Right?
sentences.zh: 我爱我父母，但我也看了看上一代人，对吧？

sentences.en: You go to Walmart, you look around, you see the people, and you're like, that's not what I want my life to end up as.
sentences.zh: 你去 Walmart，环顾四周，看到那些人，你就会想，我不想我的人生最后变成这样。

sentences.en: And when I reverse engineered, okay.
sentences.zh: 然后我就在脑子里倒推，好吧。

sentences.en: What led them to that in my head as a teenager?
sentences.zh: 在我那个青少年脑袋里，是什么让他们走到了那一步？

sentences.en: It's like 9 to 5 job, right?
sentences.zh: 就是朝九晚五的工作，对吧？

sentences.en: That takes up most of your day. You get home at night, you're super tired.
sentences.zh: 它占掉了你一天的大部分时间。你晚上回到家，累得要死。

sentences.en: You don't really get to work on something meaningful.
sentences.zh: 你根本没机会去做一些有意义的事。

sentences.en: So I wanted to do something creative.
sentences.zh: 所以我想做一些创造性的事。

sentences.en: I didn't want to work at 9 to 5, and I wanted to do something creative.
sentences.zh: 我不想朝九晚五地工作，我想做一些创造性的事。

sentences.en: And I did end up going to college for five years, but I was kind of treating it as a buffer period to just experiment with things.
sentences.zh: 我后来确实去上了五年大学，但我基本把它当成一个缓冲期，用来尝试各种东西。

sentences.en: I was a straight A student in high school, but when I was in college I was the sees get degrees, dude.
sentences.zh: 我高中是全 A 学生，但到了大学，我就是那种"及格万岁"的人。

sentences.en: And so five years into college and just switching around so much, that was a theme of my youth, I guess, is I just switched around so many different times.
sentences.zh: 所以大学五年，加上不停地换来换去，这大概就是我青春期的主题，我就是不停地切换方向。

sentences.en: I just changed, I made mistakes, I pivoted, I experimented, and that gave me a lot of experience, but it also gave me a lot of failures.
sentences.zh: 我就是一直在变，我犯过错，我转过向，我做过实验，这给了我很多经验，但也给了我很多失败。

sentences.en: And at that time I was probably like $20,000 in student debt.
sentences.zh: 那时候我大概欠了两万美元的学生贷款。

sentences.en: And that continued to stack up.
sentences.zh: 而且这个数字还在继续往上堆。

sentences.en: So out of urgency and out of honestly just being scared that I wasn't going to be able to survive.
sentences.zh: 所以出于紧迫感，也出于真的害怕自己活不下去。

sentences.en: I started applying for jobs, and I got a job at a web design agency because I had previously acquired that skill.
sentences.zh: 我开始找工作，然后在一家网页设计公司找到了工作，因为我之前已经掌握了这个技能。

sentences.en: And so at that job, it was kind of a cushy job.
sentences.zh: 那份工作算是挺舒服的。

sentences.en: I just continued to learn how to freelance. Right.
sentences.zh: 我继续学习怎么自由职业。对吧。

sentences.en: I was doing web design.
sentences.zh: 我在做网页设计。

sentences.en: I could see inside of the agency that I was working at how things were kind of pieced together.
sentences.zh: 我能看到我工作的那家公司内部是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: It kind of made sense to me how to start freelancing in a good way.
sentences.zh: 我大概搞明白了怎么用正确的方式开始自由职业。

sentences.en: And so I started doing that.
sentences.zh: 于是我就开始做了。

sentences.en: And long story short, that started to pick up over the course of six, seven, eight months.
sentences.zh: 长话短说，在接下来的六七、八个月里，这件事开始有了起色。

sentences.en: And after like nine months of me working the job, I was able to quit because I felt secure enough with my freelancing job.
sentences.zh: 工作大概九个月之后，我就能辞职了，因为我对自己的自由职业收入有了足够的安全感。

sentences.en: Now, because freelancing is really just a glorified 9 to 5 job, you're still working for other people on projects that aren't yours.
sentences.zh: 不过，自由职业其实只是一种被美化的朝九晚五，你还是在为别人做不属于你的项目。

sentences.en: Probably projects that you don't care about that you don't have any creative direction in.
sentences.zh: 很可能是你不在乎的项目，你在里面没有任何创意主导权。

sentences.en: But that's aside the point. Actually not really.
sentences.zh: 但这有点跑题了。其实也不算跑题。

sentences.en: That's why I started on social media is because I saw other I don't know why I was on Twitter of all places, but I was scrolling and I saw that there were other web designers and people talking about my interest.
sentences.zh: 这就是我为什么开始在社交媒体上发声，因为我看到了其他人——我也不知道为什么偏偏是 Twitter，但我刷的时候看到有其他网页设计师和人在聊我感兴趣的东西。

sentences.en: The web designers were just giving out basic advice, right?
sentences.zh: 那些网页设计师只是在分享一些基础建议，对吧？

sentences.en: They were like saying, here's the top ten skills that you need to learn if you want to quit your job.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，如果你想辞职，这是你需要学的十大技能。

sentences.en: And to me, that resonated at the time.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这在当时引起了共鸣。

sentences.en: But they were landing web design clients from that, and they were selling courses on how to do web design, how to freelance, other things like that.
sentences.zh: 但他们通过这个接到了网页设计的客户，还在卖课程，教人怎么做网页设计、怎么自由职业，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so I'm like, I can do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我就想，我也能做同样的事。

sentences.en: They're saying all of the things that I know how to say and they're doing really well.
sentences.zh: 他们说的那些东西我都会说，而且他们做得非常好。

sentences.en: Why am I not in their position?
sentences.zh: 为什么我不在他们的位置上？

sentences.en: So I started posting on social media, but my edge and the way I kind of had consistent growth out of the gate, it wasn't super fast all at once.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始在社交媒体上发内容，但我的优势，以及我从一开始就能持续增长的方式——并不是一下子就超级快。

sentences.en: It was kind of like 100 followers a week for two months, and then it picked up to like 500 followers a week, and then kind of stabilized around 2000 followers a month.
sentences.zh: 大概是前两个月每周涨 100 个粉丝，然后涨到每周 500 个粉丝，之后稳定在每月 2000 个粉丝左右。

sentences.en: And then there were waves.
sentences.zh: 然后会有波动。

sentences.en: There was like large explosions of follower growth when I had a tweet do really well.
sentences.zh: 当我有一条推文爆了的时候，粉丝增长会出现大爆发。

sentences.en: And then there was just the troughs of like of 1500 to 2000 followers a month, and it was pretty stable.
sentences.zh: 然后也会有低谷，大概每月 1500 到 2000 个粉丝，相当稳定。

sentences.en: But the reason I was able to do that is because my failures in digital art taught me brand esthetics to some degree, right?
sentences.zh: 但我能做到这一点的原因，是我在数字艺术上的失败经历，在某种程度上教会了我品牌美学，对吧？

sentences.en: All of skill acquisition is really just pattern recognition.
sentences.zh: 所有的技能习得，本质上只是模式识别。

sentences.en: So it's not like I was actually practicing or doing the skill when I was growing on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说我在 Twitter 上增长的时候，真的在练习或运用那个技能。

sentences.en: It's more so I had just like failed and had so much experience under my belt already that I had better taste out of the gate for what a hook looked like, because I had studied Facebook ads and copywriting when I was trying to make the agencies work that I had, I did some cold outreach.
sentences.zh: 更像是，我已经失败过，积累了足够多的经验，所以从一开始就对什么是好的钩子有更好的品味，因为我之前试图让我的代理公司运转起来的时候，研究过 Facebook 广告和文案写作，我也做过一些冷启动的外联。

sentences.en: I knew how to network, I knew how to DM people. I knew how to make friends.
sentences.zh: 我知道怎么建立人脉，我知道怎么私信别人。我知道怎么交朋友。

sentences.en: I knew how to provide a value so that they would provide value in return, which we're going to talk about in this video.
sentences.zh: 我知道怎么提供价值，这样他们也会回报价值，这个我们会在视频里讲到。

sentences.en: When I finally get to the point and the web design that I was doing paired with the copywriting really well, paired with the branding really well.
sentences.zh: 等我终于讲到重点的时候，你会发现，我在做的网页设计，和文案写作结合得非常好，和品牌塑造结合得也非常好。

sentences.en: And so I was off to a better start when it came to learning how to create digital products or just creating digital products better than most beginners, because what most people do when they start on social media is that's their first endeavor, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在学习如何创建数字产品，或者说只是比大多数新手更好地创建数字产品这件事上，我有了一个更好的起点，因为大多数人在社交媒体上起步时，那是他们的第一次尝试，对吧？

sentences.en: So they're learning the skills as they go in there, building up taste over time.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一边做一边学技能，慢慢培养品味。

sentences.en: And that's kind of what gets you stuck in beginner hell.
sentences.zh: 而这恰恰是让你困在新手地狱的原因。

sentences.en: Beginner hell is where you kind of you just post into the void and you don't really gain any followers.
sentences.zh: 新手地狱就是，你对着虚空发内容，却根本涨不了粉。

sentences.en: And usually if you don't correct your mistakes or you don't pay attention to what's working and what's not, and you don't course correct and iterate, then you're never really going to have your breakout.
sentences.zh: 通常如果你不纠正错误，不去关注什么有效什么无效，不调整方向、不迭代，那你就永远不会有突破。

sentences.en: And that's why most creators, and I don't blame them, quit because they just can't gain any traction.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么大多数创作者——我不怪他们——会放弃，因为他们就是无法获得任何增长。

sentences.en: So that's my goal with this video.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我做这个视频的目的。

sentences.en: Social media is a very viable business model, especially for one person, especially with AI on your side.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体是一个非常可行的商业模式，尤其对一个人来说，尤其当你有 AI 助阵的时候。

sentences.en: Like, you can build so many cool things in today's world, and if you have the skills that allow you to stand out because most people are just going the route of, oh, I need to post content, or I need to build something with AI, everyone's doing that, and if everyone's doing it, then like nobody's nobody's going to succeed doing that.
sentences.zh: 在当今世界，你可以做出很多很酷的东西，但前提是你有让你脱颖而出的技能，因为大多数人只会走那条路：哦，我得发内容，或者我得用 AI 做点什么，所有人都在做，如果所有人都在做，那就没人能靠这个成功。

sentences.en: Yes, AI gives you superpowers, but when everyone has superpowers, nobody has superpowers.
sentences.zh: 没错，AI 给你超能力，但当人人都有超能力时，就没人有超能力了。

sentences.en: So again, that's my goal.
sentences.zh: 所以，重申一遍，这就是我的目的。

sentences.en: You're not going to avoid the failure.
sentences.zh: 你躲不开失败。

sentences.en: You're not going to avoid the mistakes.
sentences.zh: 你躲不开犯错。

sentences.en: You're not going to avoid having to build up the experience that leads to pattern recognition.
sentences.zh: 你躲不开必须积累经验，才能形成模式识别。

sentences.en: That leads to skill acquisition.
sentences.zh: 才能获得技能。

sentences.en: But what I can tell you is the two levers that you actually need to pull to see social media growth faster, and it will help with pattern recognition faster.
sentences.zh: 但我能告诉你的是，有两个杠杆是你真正需要去拉动的，才能更快看到社交媒体增长，而且这也会帮你更快形成模式识别。

sentences.en: My secondary goal with this video is to show you that social media isn't luck based on an algorithm.
sentences.zh: 我做这个视频的第二个目的，是让你看到，社交媒体不是靠算法碰运气。

sentences.en: You don't just post and hope that the algorithm picks you up, and then blame the algorithm for your failure and your lack of skill.
sentences.zh: 你不是只管发内容，然后祈祷算法选中你，再把你的失败和技能不足怪到算法头上。

sentences.en: Social media is like a video game.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体就像一款电子游戏。

sentences.en: Many things are like a video game.
sentences.zh: 很多事情都像电子游戏。

sentences.en: They have specific mechanics and levers you can learn and pull.
sentences.zh: 它们有特定的机制和杠杆，你可以学习、可以去拉动。

sentences.en: And when you're at a higher level in the video game, you kind of see it all.
sentences.zh: 当你在游戏里等级更高时，你基本上能看清全局。

sentences.en: You've already gone through all the mechanics, you have already leveled up all of the abilities.
sentences.zh: 你已经走通了所有机制，已经把所有能力都升满了。

sentences.en: It's just like you get to be more creative.
sentences.zh: 你就可以更自由地去创造。

sentences.en: But when you're an expert at something, usually you have more.
sentences.zh: 但当你成为某个领域的专家时，通常你拥有更多。

sentences.en: You have more potential for shiny object syndrome, and you need to focus more.
sentences.zh: 你也更容易陷入新奇事物综合征，你需要更专注。

sentences.en: So as a beginner, you actually have an advantage over people, because the people who are very good at social media also tend to fall off.
sentences.zh: 所以作为新手，你其实比其他人更有优势，因为那些很擅长社交媒体的人也往往会掉队。

sentences.en: You see a lot of big YouTubers or people just like decrease output.
sentences.zh: 你会看到很多大 YouTuber 或者其他人，产出量就是下降了。

sentences.en: I've decreased output lately, and what that does is it opens up space for new creators to come in.
sentences.zh: 我最近产出也下降了，而这带来的结果是，为新创作者腾出了空间。

sentences.en: So two levers.
sentences.zh: 所以，两个杠杆。

sentences.en: That's what we need to know.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们需要知道的。

sentences.en: Treat everything else as a distraction.
sentences.zh: 把其他一切都当作干扰。

sentences.en: Literally just focus on these two things.
sentences.zh: 真的就只专注这两件事。

sentences.en: Don't get distracted.
sentences.zh: 别分心。

sentences.en: Focus on these two things and you will do just fine, I promise.
sentences.zh: 专注这两件事，你一定会做得很好，我保证。

sentences.en: So the first lever is to do what works from your own perspective.
sentences.zh: 第一个杠杆是：从你自己的视角出发，做那些已经被验证有效的事。

sentences.en: And that sounds kind of that doesn't sound that great just yet, but I promise, like, this is the secret.
sentences.zh: 这话乍一听可能没什么感觉，但我保证，这就是秘密。

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: If you actually treat it as a priority, it will become a priority.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的把它当成优先事项，它就会变成优先事项。

sentences.en: Because a big problem that beginner creators have is like they always think, oh, I don't have anything new to say.
sentences.zh: 新手创作者有个很大的问题，他们总觉得：唉，我没什么新东西可说。

sentences.en: As if people are on social media to see something new.
sentences.zh: 好像人们上社交媒体是为了看新东西似的。

sentences.en: They're not.
sentences.zh: 他们不是。

sentences.en: If you actually think about how you consume social media or how I consume social media, people are there to see what's already being talked about from a specific creator's opinion.
sentences.zh: 你仔细想想自己是怎么刷社交媒体的，或者我是怎么刷的——人们去那里，是想看某个特定创作者对已经有人在讨论的话题有什么看法。

sentences.en: That's literally how the algorithm works, especially YouTube.
sentences.zh: 算法的运作方式就是这样，YouTube 尤其如此。

sentences.en: If you watch one video on a specific topic, YouTube is going to show you the same fricking topic from another creator.
sentences.zh: 你只要看了一个特定主题的视频，YouTube 就会给你推另一个创作者做的、同一个他妈的主题。

sentences.en: And if you understand that, you understand if that you create a video similar to one that has already done well, then you're going to be recommended to the people who viewed the one that did.
sentences.zh: 如果你理解了这一点，你就会明白：只要你做一个跟某个已经爆过的视频类似的视频，你就会被推荐给看过那个爆款视频的人。

sentences.en: Well, I'll explain that soon, but I hope that really clicks.
sentences.zh: 这个我稍后会解释，但我希望你能真正领悟到这一点。

sentences.en: That's YouTube growth in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 这就是 YouTube 增长的终极概括。

sentences.en: Every other course, like all the other tactics, are secondary.
sentences.zh: 其他所有课程、所有别的技巧，都是次要的。

sentences.en: They're useful, but they're secondary.
sentences.zh: 它们有用，但只是次要的。

sentences.en: And it lines up with my own consumption habits.
sentences.zh: 这跟我自己的消费习惯完全吻合。

sentences.en: Like, I could see the same video title every single day from a different creator, and I would probably watch it.
sentences.zh: 比如，我可以每天看到同一个视频标题，只是出自不同创作者，而我大概率还是会点进去看。

sentences.en: I do watch it because I want to hear their opinion.
sentences.zh: 我确实会看，因为我想听听他们的观点。

sentences.en: Everyone's talking about Claude, Code, Claude, OpenAI, all of this shit, the future of work.
sentences.zh: 所有人都在聊 Claude Code、Claude、OpenAI，所有这些破事，未来的工作。

sentences.en: When I fall down a rabbit hole of wanting to learn about that, I'm just going to watch the same topic over and over again so that I get all of the nuances so that I understand it completely.
sentences.zh: 当我掉进一个想了解这些东西的兔子洞时，我就会一遍又一遍地看同一个主题，这样我才能捕捉到所有细微差别，彻底搞懂。

sentences.en: The same goes for like fitness videos on YouTube.
sentences.zh: YouTube 上的健身视频也是一样。

sentences.en: That's I'm I love fitness, like that's my honestly my main priority.
sentences.zh: 我热爱健身，老实说，那才是我真正的第一优先级。

sentences.en: This has all become secondary.
sentences.zh: 现在这些都已经变成次要的了。

sentences.en: But if I had an ounce of muscle for every time that I've watched a nutrition 101 video or just some creator's opinion on nutrition, I'd be Ronnie Coleman.
sentences.zh: 但如果我每看一次营养学 101 视频、或者某个创作者对营养学的看法就能长一盎司肌肉，我早就变成 Ronnie Coleman 了。

sentences.en: This is the single most fundamental aspect of social media growth on any platform.
sentences.zh: 这是所有平台上社交媒体增长最根本的一个要素。

sentences.en: So if we look at someone like Craig Perry, who is just running my playbook, I don't know if he got it from me, but his YouTube bio is literally reading my newsletters to a camera.
sentences.zh: 我们来看 Craig Perry 这个例子，他就是在执行我的打法——我不知道他是不是从我这里学的，但他的 YouTube 简介写的就是：对着镜头读我的 newsletter。

sentences.en: I just had my newsletter open here.
sentences.zh: 我刚才正好开着我的 newsletter。

sentences.en: It's not like I read it word for word, but it's like an outline that I can riff off of.
sentences.zh: 也不是说逐字逐句地读，而是把它当成一个提纲，我可以顺着往下发挥。

sentences.en: But if we look here, these are his first two YouTube videos ever, ever.
sentences.zh: 但我们来看看这里，这是他 YouTube 频道的前两个视频，有史以来头两个。

sentences.en: Like, do you see this?
sentences.zh: 你看到了吗？

sentences.en: You have 230 K views and you have 144 kvue's. That's literally absurd.
sentences.zh: 一个 23 万播放，一个 14.4 万播放，这简直离谱。

sentences.en: Like, you do not see that for the first two videos on someone's YouTube channel.
sentences.zh: 你在别人的 YouTube 频道上，根本看不到前两个视频就有这种数据。

sentences.en: And that proves exactly what I'm talking about here.
sentences.zh: 而这恰恰证明了我正在说的这件事。

sentences.en: Did he get lucky a bit?
sentences.zh: 他有没有一点运气成分？

sentences.en: Maybe if you were to copy these 1 to 1, would you get the same results?
sentences.zh: 也许你原封不动照搬这些，能得到同样的结果吗？

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许。

sentences.en: Maybe not, I don't know, but all I do know is that if you do this enough times, you will start to see a green streak of engagement and followers coming in.
sentences.zh: 也许不会，我不知道，但我唯一知道的是，如果你重复做这件事足够多次，你就会开始看到一条绿色的互动和关注者增长曲线。

sentences.en: So how is he doing?
sentences.zh: 那他是怎么做的？

sentences.en: What works from his own perspective?
sentences.zh: 从他自己的视角来看，什么有效？

sentences.en: If you look here how to remember everything you read.
sentences.zh: 你看这个，如何记住你读过的所有东西。

sentences.en: If you're on this side, I've created a video like that I've almost created with the exact same title.
sentences.zh: 如果你看这边，我做过一个类似的视频，标题几乎一模一样。

sentences.en: If you look on YouTube, you can see that all the Abdol has created a video like that.
sentences.zh: 如果你去 YouTube 上看，你会发现 Abdol 也做过类似的视频。

sentences.en: You can see.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到。

sentences.en: Just look up how to remember everything you read in the YouTube search bar, and you'll see like 10 to 20 iterations of those videos.
sentences.zh: 只要在 YouTube 搜索栏里搜"如何记住你读过的所有东西"，你会看到大概 10 到 20 个不同版本的视频。

sentences.en: And then right here how to become dangerously Self-educated.
sentences.zh: 然后这里，如何成为危险的自我教育者。

sentences.en: Now this one is actually kind of unique, but it uses the same validated structure because I've seen multiple times how to become dangerously articulate, how to become dangerously confident.
sentences.zh: 这个其实有点独特，但它用了同样的经过验证的结构，因为我见过很多次"如何成为危险的表达者"、"如何成为危险的自信者"。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: This is a rather new structure with the whole dangerously, but it still shows that it works.
sentences.zh: 这个"危险的"结构算是比较新的，但它仍然证明了它有效。

sentences.en: Now is this copying?
sentences.zh: 那这算抄袭吗？

sentences.en: Are the things inside of Craig's videos the same exact script that every single other person who created a how to remember Everything you read video the same?
sentences.zh: Craig 视频里的内容，跟其他每一个做过"如何记住你读过的所有东西"视频的人，用的是完全一样的脚本吗？

sentences.en: No it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不是。

sentences.en: If you actually watch the video, there's some great insights he's pulling from his own experience, from his own perspective.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的去看那个视频，里面有一些很棒的洞见，是他从自己的经验、自己的视角里提炼出来的。

sentences.en: It's his own opinion on how to do it.
sentences.zh: 是他自己关于怎么做的观点。

sentences.en: Another thing for people who are worried about copying you like nobody has a novel idea, novel ideas are extremely rare.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，对于那些担心抄袭的人，你要知道，没有人拥有全新的想法，全新的想法极其罕见。

sentences.en: It's not like Craig or I can claim how to remember everything you read like that's a process.
sentences.zh: Craig 或者我，都不能声称"如何记住你读过的所有东西"是我们的，那是一个过程。

sentences.en: That's not something that you can claim.
sentences.zh: 那不是你可以声称拥有的东西。

sentences.en: Now, if it's something else, like a unique category or a unique concept that you've created, then yes, it is kind of copying if you take it.
sentences.zh: 但如果是别的东西，比如你创造的一个独特类别或独特概念，那如果你拿走了，确实算是某种抄袭。

sentences.en: But of course, then semantics come into play.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这时候语义学就起作用了。

sentences.en: Like I did a spin off of Tim Ferriss The Four Hour Work Week.
sentences.zh: 比如我对 Tim Ferriss 的《每周工作四小时》做了一个变体。

sentences.en: I did the four hour work day because I kind of created a little framework around it from my own experience, and other people could take the four hour work day, and some people may attribute it to me, but honestly, I wouldn't be very mad because it's like, I can't claim that.
sentences.zh: 我做了"每天工作四小时"，因为我从自己的经验里围绕它建立了一个小框架，而其他人也可以拿走"每天工作四小时"，有些人可能会把它归功于我，但说实话，我不会很生气，因为我没法声称拥有它。

sentences.en: So you kind of have to use your own judgment here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里你得用自己的判断力。

sentences.en: Like if you're obviously just purely copying, then yeah, don't do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你明显就是在纯粹抄袭，那确实，别那么做。

sentences.en: But still, like an artist is a thing for a reason is because that's just how nature and reality works.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，"艺术家偷师"这句话存在是有原因的，因为这就是自然和现实的运作方式。

sentences.en: You don't reinvent the wheel.
sentences.zh: 你不会去重新发明轮子。

sentences.en: And the same thing goes with like tweets or short form posts or reels.
sentences.zh: 同样的道理也适用于推文、短视频帖子或者 Reels。

sentences.en: Like nobody can claim the idea that they're saying because it's usually not completely novel.
sentences.zh: 没有人能声称他们说的那个想法是他们的，因为它通常不是完全原创的。

sentences.en: The way that they worded it, the way that they structured it can be considered theirs.
sentences.zh: 他们表达的方式、他们构建的方式，可以被认为是他们的。

sentences.en: And obviously, like you're going to look like an idiot if you just, like, copy paste it, change a few words, which I've seen a few times, and when I see those, I kind of immediately label that person as like, wow, you can't think originally, but you can take the idea.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，如果你只是复制粘贴、改几个词，你会看起来像个傻子，我见过几次这种情况，当我看到那些的时候，我几乎立刻就会给那个人贴上标签：哇，你完全没有原创思考能力。但你可以拿走那个想法。

sentences.en: So I mean, if we just look at these posts here, like major cheat code for life, increase your recovery speed, you will get rejected.
sentences.zh: 所以你看这些帖子，比如"人生重大作弊码"、"提升你的恢复速度"、"你会被拒绝"。

sentences.en: You will lose money, you will embarrass yourself.
sentences.zh: 你会亏钱，你会让自己难堪。

sentences.en: The goal isn't to avoid the fall.
sentences.zh: 目标不是避免跌倒。

sentences.en: It's to shorten the time between the fall and the reset.
sentences.zh: 而是缩短跌倒和重新站起来之间的时间。

sentences.en: Fast recovery compounds.
sentences.zh: 快速恢复会复利增长。

sentences.en: Now there's an essence to this idea, obviously.
sentences.zh: 这个想法显然有它的核心精髓。

sentences.en: Like saying increase your recovery speed.
sentences.zh: 比如"提升你的恢复速度"这句话。

sentences.en: That's kind of Saul Bloom coded, but major T code for life.
sentences.zh: 有点 Saul Bloom 的味道，但"人生重大作弊码"就很吸睛。

sentences.en: You could definitely use that as a hook. Why not?
sentences.zh: 你完全可以用它做钩子。为什么不用呢？

sentences.en: And then if you actually look at this tweet, you can just read into it and be like, you will get rejected, you will lose money.
sentences.zh: 然后你仔细看这条推文，读进去就会想到：你会被拒绝，你会亏钱。

sentences.en: And then you start to think, do other ideas spin off of that?
sentences.zh: 接着你开始思考，会不会有其他想法从这里衍生出来？

sentences.en: And most of the time they do.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候会的。

sentences.en: And one thing I like to actually use AI for is just that for iterations on those ideas, because like, I can think through them and let ideas come to my mind, but when I'm actually sitting down to write a post like you kind of need a topic to write about, you don't necessarily need to brainstorm and like, have this non practical way of coming up with an idea or reject AI, like you're just trying to choose a topic to write about so that then you can think, you can think in a certain direction.
sentences.zh: 有一件事我其实喜欢用 AI 来做，就是对这些想法进行迭代。因为我可以自己想通，让想法自然浮现，但当我真正坐下来写帖子时，你总得有个主题来写。你不一定需要去头脑风暴，用那种不切实际的方式想点子，或者排斥 AI。你只是在选一个要写的主题，这样你才能思考，才能朝着某个方向去想。

sentences.en: So what I like to do is take really good posts that I like and be like, hey, just give me iterations of these and I'll read through them and I'll just wait for one to hit and I'll be like, okay, yeah, I'll write about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢做的是，拿一些我喜欢的优质帖子，然后说，嘿，给我一些迭代版本。我会通读它们，等着某一个击中我，然后我就说，好，就写这个。

sentences.en: And usually through so many, through those two filters of like, okay, goes through AI to give me a iteration, it goes through my mind because I'm usually not taking exactly what it says here.
sentences.zh: 通常经过这么多层——经过这两层过滤：一层是 AI 给我一个迭代版本，一层是我的大脑，因为我通常不会直接照搬它给的东西。

sentences.en: By the end of that process, I usually have something that's pretty original.
sentences.zh: 到这个过程的结尾，我通常就有了相当原创的东西。

sentences.en: And since I've read and pattern recognized and pattern matched so many good posts, the structure of my writing starts to come out over time, and then I can use my own taste to refine it to make it even further mine.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我读过、识别过、匹配过那么多优质帖子的模式，我的写作结构会随着时间自然浮现，然后我可以用自己的品味去打磨它，让它更进一步成为我的东西。

sentences.en: So that's like that's content 101 in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上就是内容创作 101。

sentences.en: Now, an even better way to just lock this in is many of you remember this video, how to get ahead of 99% of people in 6 to 12 months?
sentences.zh: 现在，一个更好的巩固方法——你们很多人记得这个视频：《如何在 6 到 12 个月内领先 99% 的人》。

sentences.en: What many of you don't know is that I wrote a tweet in 2019 or 2020.
sentences.zh: 很多人不知道的是，我在 2019 年还是 2020 年写过一条推文。

sentences.en: I think it's 2019 with the first line that said, how to get ahead of 99% of people.
sentences.zh: 我记得是 2019 年，第一句就是"如何领先 99% 的人"。

sentences.en: So it was already a validated idea in 2023.
sentences.zh: 所以到 2023 年，这已经是一个被验证过的想法了。

sentences.en: I turned it into that YouTube video.
sentences.zh: 我把它变成了那个 YouTube 视频。

sentences.en: That's now my highest performing YouTube video at 1.7 million views.
sentences.zh: 现在那是我表现最好的 YouTube 视频，170 万次观看。

sentences.en: After that, video did really well.
sentences.zh: 那个视频火了之后。

sentences.en: Mark Manson, the author of The Subtle Art of Not Giving a Fuck, created a video with the same exact title, except he said something else instead of in six months, and that video got like 4.5 million views.
sentences.zh: Mark Manson，《不在乎的精妙艺术》的作者，做了一个标题完全一样的视频，只是他把"在六个月内"换成了别的说法，那个视频拿到了大概 450 万次观看。

sentences.en: It's a proven topic, at least for now, until it gets ran through.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被验证过的主题，至少目前是这样，直到它被用烂。

sentences.en: That's another thing is you'll eventually learn that some topics that used to do well are kind of just dead now, or they've been exhausted to the point where they need a reset period, and you'll see how to get ahead of 99% of people start to come back up in maybe a year, two years, and it'll flood the space, it'll be super viral for a second and then it'll die down.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，你最终会学到，有些曾经很火的主题现在已经死了，或者被榨干到需要一个冷却期。你会看到"如何领先 99% 的人"这个主题可能过一两年又会回来，然后它会淹没整个圈子，超级病毒式传播一阵子，然后又沉寂下去。

sentences.en: But after Mark Manson made the video, Alex Hermosa made a video titled How to Get Ahead of 99% of people.
sentences.zh: 但在 Mark Manson 做了那个视频之后，Alex Hermosa 做了一个视频，标题就是《如何领先 99% 的人》。

sentences.en: And then after that, Tom Bellew retitled one of his videos to have how to get ahead of 99% of people in the title.
sentences.zh: 再之后，Tom Bellew 把他其中一个视频的标题改成了包含"如何领先 99% 的人"。

sentences.en: So that's four massive creators who just prove what I'm saying here.
sentences.zh: 所以这是四个大创作者，正好印证了我说的。

sentences.en: And that's the thing, is that these creators aren't creating the same exact video.
sentences.zh: 关键是，这些创作者做的不是完全一样的视频。

sentences.en: In my video, I'm talking about, like the process of creating an anti vision and a vision and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 在我的视频里，我讲的是创建反愿景和愿景的过程之类的东西。

sentences.en: But Mark Manson, like he's written so much about this before that he is a completely different view, right?
sentences.zh: 但 Mark Manson，他之前已经写过太多这方面的内容，所以他有完全不同的视角，对吧？

sentences.en: Anyone can take the topic how to be, how to get ahead of 99% of people and just think, how would I get ahead of 99% of people based on my interest, right?
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以拿"如何超越99%的人"这个话题，然后去想：基于我的兴趣，我会怎么超越99%的人，对吧？

sentences.en: It doesn't even like it can be business.
sentences.zh: 它甚至不一定是商业。

sentences.en: It can be start a business like this to get ahead of 99% of people.
sentences.zh: 可以是"像这样创业，超越99%的人"。

sentences.en: It could be finance budget like this.
sentences.zh: 可以是"像这样理财做预算"。

sentences.en: It could be relationships. How to get ahead of 99% of men.
sentences.zh: 可以是人际关系。"如何超越99%的男人"。

sentences.en: Because for some reason, young men just compete against each other and look smacks all day and don't really get anywhere with it.
sentences.zh: 因为不知道为什么，年轻男人整天互相较劲、互相嘲讽，却什么结果都没搞出来。

sentences.en: But they'll learn that lesson when they get to it.
sentences.zh: 但他们到了那个阶段自然会学到这一课。

sentences.en: But the point, the overarching point is that the best creators don't just post what's on their mind, right?
sentences.zh: 但重点是，最核心的一点是：最好的创作者不只是把脑子里想的东西发出来，对吧？

sentences.en: They don't just, like, open up their phone and send a post.
sentences.zh: 他们不会只是打开手机就发一条帖子。

sentences.en: Some do, I do.
sentences.zh: 有些人会，我也会。

sentences.en: Sometimes you should, but that shouldn't. That's not a strategy, right?
sentences.zh: 有时候你应该这么做，但那不是策略，对吧？

sentences.en: If you're treating social media as a way to pursue your life's work, then business is a part of that practicality strategy, tactics.
sentences.zh: 如果你把社交媒体当作追求你毕生事业的方式，那商业就是其中的一部分——实操、策略、战术。

sentences.en: So the best creators most of the time research what works and base what they're going to create about on that.
sentences.zh: 所以最好的创作者大多数时候会研究什么有效，然后基于那个来决定自己要创作什么。

sentences.en: And so what most people do here is they'll just like bookmark posts on social media and hope that they come back to it and remember it when it's time to actually create.
sentences.zh: 而大多数人在这里的做法是：在社交媒体上收藏帖子，然后指望自己回头会去看、会在真正创作的时候想起来。

sentences.en: But then most people just start looking at a blank page and write something that isn't that good, and then wonder why it didn't do well since they're actually doing the steps, or before they write the YouTube title, they'll go to YouTube and they'll search for similar titles, and that's a solid way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 但接着大多数人就盯着空白页面开始写，写出来的东西不怎么样，然后纳闷为什么没火——明明自己按步骤做了。或者在写YouTube标题之前，他们会去YouTube搜类似的标题，这倒是个靠谱的做法。

sentences.en: Or they'll go to the creator's account and filter by most popular, and then they can write down and study those specific titles that did well.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会去那个创作者的账号，按最热门排序，然后把那些表现好的标题记下来研究。

sentences.en: Another thing people do is they just jot down ideas as they come to mind, and hope that those ideas are good enough to do well.
sentences.zh: 人们还会做的另一件事是：脑子里冒出什么想法就随手记下来，然后指望那些想法足够好、能火。

sentences.en: And sometimes they are, and all of those are fine, but they're not really strategized.
sentences.zh: 有时候确实能火，这些做法都没问题，但它们没有真正的策略性。

sentences.en: They're not really a system.
sentences.zh: 它们算不上一个系统。

sentences.en: They're not something that you can rely on.
sentences.zh: 它们不是你可以依赖的东西。

sentences.en: And frankly, they're just time consuming and they're slow.
sentences.zh: 而且说实话，这些做法很耗时间、很慢。

sentences.en: And so this is where I transition into a sales pitch for the new iteration of Eden, which is very focused on outlier content and just being the place where you research content and write great content.
sentences.zh: 所以这里我要过渡到新版Eden的介绍——它非常专注于异类内容，就是让你研究内容、写出好内容的地方。

sentences.en: Eden is quite literally, you have boards that you can paste links to of social posts or websites, or you can upload PDFs to.
sentences.zh: Eden说白了就是：你有看板，可以把社交媒体帖子或网站的链接粘贴进去，也可以上传PDF。

sentences.en: You can create notes in or documents.
sentences.zh: 你可以在里面创建笔记或文档。

sentences.en: So you can write.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以写作。

sentences.en: And so it's like I showed you my YouTube swipe file.
sentences.zh: 就像我给你看了我的YouTube素材库。

sentences.en: I showed you the post swipe file. I can reference these with AI.
sentences.zh: 我给你看了帖子素材库。我可以用AI来参考这些内容。

sentences.en: Or I can go to the discover feed, set my content pillars, and then I can just scroll through here and see which post catch my eye.
sentences.zh: 或者我可以去发现信息流，设置好我的内容支柱，然后直接在这里滑动浏览，看哪些帖子吸引我。

sentences.en: I can also filter by platform if I only want to see tweets or YouTube videos, and then I can click one when I like it.
sentences.zh: 我还可以按平台筛选，只看推文或YouTube视频，然后看到喜欢的就点进去。

sentences.en: Let's say I add this one to my YouTube swipe file.
sentences.zh: 比如说我把这条加到我的YouTube素材库里。

sentences.en: Boom! Add it there.
sentences.zh: Boom！加进去。

sentences.en: So if you don't know what to create next, just scroll through here, add it to a board, and then when it's time to actually create, go to your board, create a note in there, and then start writing.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不知道接下来该创作什么，就在这里滑动浏览，加到看板里，然后到了真正要创作的时候，去你的看板，在里面创建一个笔记，然后开始写。

sentences.en: Another thing that you won't find anywhere else is just the ability to search a specific creator and look at all of their platforms and filter by top performing content.
sentences.zh: 还有一个你在别处找不到的功能：直接搜索某个创作者，查看他所有平台的内容，并按表现最好的内容筛选。

sentences.en: So a lot of mine on Twitter are articles, so Twitter just renders those as a link.
sentences.zh: 我在Twitter上的很多内容是文章，Twitter就把那些渲染成一个链接。

sentences.en: But I can scroll through here and I can just see one my own good ideas so I can iterate off of those.
sentences.zh: 但我可以在这里翻看，一眼就能看到自己以前的好点子，然后在此基础上迭代。

sentences.en: And I do that all the time.
sentences.zh: 我一直都这么做。

sentences.en: That's really how I continue growing at this point.
sentences.zh: 这就是我现阶段能持续成长的核心方式。

sentences.en: But I can save a bunch of these two aboard and just use them as an inspiration.
sentences.zh: 但我也可以把这些内容存到看板上，纯粹当灵感来源。

sentences.en: Or you can do what I showed you earlier where if I open the post swipe file and then I open the chat and I can reference this board in the chat, and then I can ask for variations of these, or I can just chat with it, or I can add a creator's top performing YouTube videos and just be like, hey, break all of these down.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以像我刚才演示的那样，打开帖子素材库，再打开聊天窗口，在聊天里引用这个看板，然后让它生成这些内容的变体，或者直接跟它聊，或者把某个创作者表现最好的 YouTube 视频加进去，直接说：嘿，把这些全拆解一遍。

sentences.en: What is this person's worldview?
sentences.zh: 这个人的世界观是什么？

sentences.en: How does these structures videos?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么结构化视频的？

sentences.en: How can I apply this to the next video that I create?
sentences.zh: 我怎么把这些应用到我的下一个视频里？

sentences.en: Help me create that video.
sentences.zh: 帮我做出那个视频。

sentences.en: So super simple, super powerful.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单，这么强大。

sentences.en: I'm actually very excited about this new version of Eden.
sentences.zh: 我对这个新版 Eden 真的非常兴奋。

sentences.en: If you're wondering what happened to the old version of Eden, there's actually an article up that is at Eden.
sentences.zh: 如果你好奇旧版 Eden 怎么了，其实有一篇文章在 Eden 网站上。

sentences.en: So the New Eden and that kind of goes over how we went broke thanks to AI credits and how we had to pivot to something specific that is actually a lot more valuable.
sentences.zh: 就是 New Eden 那篇，大概讲了 AI 积分怎么让我们破产，以及我们如何被迫转向一个更具体、实际上也更有价值的方向。

sentences.en: And we landed on this.
sentences.zh: 最终我们做出了这个。

sentences.en: So blessing and a curse, because this is going to become a staple in what I hope is every creator's workflow.
sentences.zh: 所以是福也是祸，因为这个东西会成为——我希望——每个创作者工作流里的标配。

sentences.en: And I'm going to work to make that happen, because this is just like a massive unlock that no other app has.
sentences.zh: 我会努力让它实现，因为这是一个巨大的解锁，没有任何其他应用能做到。

sentences.en: So I'm super excited about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我超级兴奋。

sentences.en: You can try it out with the link in the description, and I think you will enjoy it quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 你可以用描述里的链接试试看，我觉得你会很喜欢。

sentences.en: Okay, onto the second lever that you can pull.
sentences.zh: 好，接下来是你可以拉动的第二个杠杆。

sentences.en: The first one is just validated content.
sentences.zh: 第一个就是经过验证的内容。

sentences.en: Study what works and create your own opinion on it.
sentences.zh: 研究什么有效，然后形成你自己的观点。

sentences.en: It is that simple.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: That's how you start practicing writing good content.
sentences.zh: 这就是你开始练习写出好内容的方式。

sentences.en: Please do not overcomplicate that.
sentences.zh: 千万别把它搞复杂了。

sentences.en: So the second lever you're going to hate this word but it's networking.
sentences.zh: 第二个杠杆，你会讨厌这个词，但就是社交。

sentences.en: And so with this I don't know what goes through most people's heads when they actually start on social media, but for some reason they're just probably bringing consumer behavior over.
sentences.zh: 说到这个，我不知道大多数人刚上社交媒体时脑子里在想什么，但出于某种原因，他们大概是把消费者行为带过来了。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: They're used to just scrolling on social media and seeing that oh, people post and oh, this posted really well.
sentences.zh: 他们习惯了在社交媒体上刷内容，看到别人发帖，看到某个帖子数据很好。

sentences.en: And so all I have to do is start creating posts, and then one will do well and then I'll become famous.
sentences.zh: 然后就觉得，我只要开始发帖，总会有一条爆的，然后我就出名了。

sentences.en: They don't see that a creator treats it as a business because that's what it is at this point.
sentences.zh: 他们看不到一个创作者把它当成生意来做，因为现阶段它就是生意。

sentences.en: But a business doesn't have to be soulless.
sentences.zh: 但生意不一定非得是冷冰冰的。

sentences.en: It can be very purposeful.
sentences.zh: 它可以非常有意义。

sentences.en: It's been the most purposeful thing in my life.
sentences.zh: 它是我人生中最有意义的事。

sentences.en: It's led to some of the most drastic changes I've had in my life, and it can actually provide good.
sentences.zh: 它带来了我人生中最剧烈的改变，而且它真的能创造价值。

sentences.en: Oh, no, you're selling something for money.
sentences.zh: 哦不，你居然在卖东西赚钱。

sentences.en: That thing, preferably for a specific person, is valuable and it's worth paying the money in.
sentences.zh: 那东西，最好是为某个特定人群打造的，是有价值的，值得别人掏钱。

sentences.en: Preferably it would be worth more than what you're charging in the value that it does provide.
sentences.zh: 而且它实际提供的价值，最好远超你收取的价格。

sentences.en: It's called voluntary exchange.
sentences.zh: 这叫自愿交换。

sentences.en: But if it were as easy as just posting, then everyone would do it.
sentences.zh: 但如果成功真像随便发发帖那么简单，那人人都会去做。

sentences.en: And then if everyone did it and then if everyone did it, then it wouldn't work for anyone.
sentences.zh: 而如果人人都去做，那这条路对任何人都不再奏效。

sentences.en: Just like AI.
sentences.zh: 就像 AI 一样。

sentences.en: Like, you have to understand that if you want to be good at something, you have to treat it as a skill that you acquire over time.
sentences.zh: 你得明白，如果你想在任何事上变得出色，就必须把它当作一项需要长期打磨的技能。

sentences.en: I don't know how that doesn't click for people, like just because it's social media.
sentences.zh: 我不懂为什么很多人就是转不过这个弯，就因为它只是社交媒体。

sentences.en: A thing that you use on your phone every single day, doesn't mean that there isn't a very high skill cap to succeeding at the business side of that thing.
sentences.zh: 一个你每天都在手机上用的东西，不代表在商业层面取得成功不需要极高的技能上限。

sentences.en: So now the question is, okay, Dan, well, what do I do if it's not just praying for the algorithm and hoping that my post goes viral?
sentences.zh: 所以现在的问题是，好吧 Dan，如果成功不是靠祈祷算法眷顾、指望帖子爆火，那我该做什么？

sentences.en: Because we learned about validated ideas, we learned how to find those.
sentences.zh: 因为我们学会了什么是经过验证的想法，也学会了如何找到它们。

sentences.en: We learned that if you create your own opinion on them, you're setting yourself up to do really well.
sentences.zh: 我们明白了，如果你能在这些想法上形成自己的观点，你就为自己铺好了成功的路。

sentences.en: But if you're in beginner hell, if you're at the very start, you're still posting into the void.
sentences.zh: 但如果你身处新手地狱，如果你才刚刚起步，你依然是在对着虚空发帖。

sentences.en: You can't expect the algorithm to just launch you into the ether and give you a ton of followers, especially on certain platforms like Twitter, where the algorithm is kind of non-existent.
sentences.zh: 你不能指望算法直接把你发射到太空，给你一堆粉丝，尤其是在像 Twitter 这样算法几乎不存在的平台上。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: I started on that platform, so I knew that my growth had to take manual effort.
sentences.zh: 我就是从那个平台起步的，所以我知道我的增长必须靠手动努力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I'm blessed that I did it that way, because now I know that, like, if the algorithm isn't working in my favor, I still have a lever I can pull.
sentences.zh: 我很庆幸自己走了那条路，因为现在我知道，就算算法不站在我这边，我依然有一个可以拉动的杠杆。

sentences.en: So let's just break this down so it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 那我们就把这事拆解清楚。

sentences.en: You want followers?
sentences.zh: 你想要粉丝？

sentences.en: Followers come from people seeing your post on their phone and then clicking your profile and being interested enough to follow you.
sentences.zh: 粉丝来源于人们在手机上看到你的帖子，然后点进你的主页，并且有足够的兴趣关注你。

sentences.en: And so if the algorithm is like the lottery, so people aren't going to see your post on their timeline organically, how can we manually get people to see your posts?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果算法就像买彩票，人们不会在时间线上自然看到你的帖子，那我们怎么手动让人们看到你的帖子？

sentences.en: How can we start rolling the snowball until it, like, starts rolling down the hill or becomes an avalanche or whatever?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么开始推动这个雪球，直到它自己滚下山，或者变成一场雪崩之类的？

sentences.en: So you have to think where is the source of followers or people on social media?
sentences.zh: 所以你必须思考，社交媒体上粉丝或人群的源头在哪里？

sentences.en: And it's in other people's audiences, right?
sentences.zh: 就在其他人的受众里，对吧？

sentences.en: When you're on social media, you really have only a few actions that you can take.
sentences.zh: 当你在社交媒体上时，你能做的动作其实就那么几个。

sentences.en: You can follow someone, you can like their post, you can repost it and you can comment on it.
sentences.zh: 你可以关注某人，可以点赞他们的帖子，可以转发，也可以评论。

sentences.en: That's the that's the bookmarks, etc. like those are all those don't matter.
sentences.zh: 还有收藏之类的，那些都不重要。

sentences.en: That's the thing you do on social media is you engage and you follow.
sentences.zh: 你在社交媒体上做的事就是互动和关注。

sentences.en: So the followers that you want lie are following someone else.
sentences.zh: 所以，你想要的粉丝，正躺在别人的关注列表里。

sentences.en: This is why brands pay so much for creators to post about their product, because they have an audience.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么品牌愿意花大价钱让创作者推广他们的产品，因为创作者有受众。

sentences.en: Like how else is the brand going to find people to buy their product?
sentences.zh: 不然品牌还能怎么找到人来买他们的产品？

sentences.en: They need to put it in front of people, and the way they can do that is like podcast sponsorships.
sentences.zh: 他们需要把产品推到人们面前，而实现这一点的方式之一就是播客赞助。

sentences.en: Partner with the creator on social media, run paid ads, Facebook or Google.
sentences.zh: 跟创作者在社交媒体上合作，投付费广告，Facebook 或 Google。

sentences.en: Maybe you run ChatGPT ads now that those are a thing, or they can do other forms of marketing.
sentences.zh: 现在 ChatGPT 广告也有了，你也可以投那个，或者用其他营销方式。

sentences.en: But on social media, as a creator, you're practically marketing yourself, so you could technically pay people to share your posts.
sentences.zh: 但在社交媒体上，作为创作者，你本质上就是在营销自己，所以严格来说你也可以花钱让人转发你的帖子。

sentences.en: And that works to some extent if you do it the correct way.
sentences.zh: 如果你用对方法，这在某种程度上是有效的。

sentences.en: But let's not bank on that.
sentences.zh: 但我们别把希望全押在这上面。

sentences.en: And for those who kind of get turned off by that, that's a very viable strategy, right?
sentences.zh: 对那些一听这个就反感的人来说，这其实是个很可行的策略，对吧？

sentences.en: If you're treating this as a business or as like a way to pursue your life's work and you have the money to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这件事当成生意，或者当成追求你毕生事业的方式，而且你有这个钱。

sentences.en: Go ahead.
sentences.zh: 那就去做。

sentences.en: I do not care because people are only going to follow you if your content is good, right?
sentences.zh: 我无所谓，因为人们只会在你的内容好的时候才会关注你，对吧？

sentences.en: If your content sucks like people say, it's cheating to pay someone else, it just doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 如果你内容很烂，就像那些人说的，花钱让别人转发就是作弊，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: They don't have a business mindset, they don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 他们没有商业思维，他们不懂。

sentences.en: But if someone else shares your post and people don't like it, they're not going to follow you and then it's a waste of money.
sentences.zh: 但如果别人转发了你的帖子，而人们不喜欢，他们就不会关注你，那钱就白花了。

sentences.en: It's the same thing as putting money into Facebook ads and people not buying your product because your product sucks.
sentences.zh: 这跟你往 Facebook 广告里砸钱，但没人买你的产品是一个道理，因为你的产品太烂了。

sentences.en: So in essence, it doesn't really matter if you pay or not, because you're only going to grow, if you're good, if you're skilled.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，你花不花钱真的不重要，因为你能增长，只取决于你够不够好，你够不够有本事。

sentences.en: But if you don't want to pay someone, and if you're smart, you can get in front of other people's audiences for free.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不想花钱请人，而且你够聪明，你可以免费出现在别人的受众面前。

sentences.en: And all of it just boils down to making friends.
sentences.zh: 而这一切归根结底就是交朋友。

sentences.en: And I know that sounds simple again, because it is.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来又很简单，因为它确实简单。

sentences.en: But most people don't know how to make friends.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人不知道怎么交朋友。

sentences.en: Most people in today's world are antisocial.
sentences.zh: 当今世界大多数人都是反社交的。

sentences.en: You would think that more people being on social media would be more social, but they're not.
sentences.zh: 你可能会以为更多人上社交媒体就会更社交，但他们并没有。

sentences.en: And so yes, that means that you're going to have to talk to people and that on social media that happens in the DMs or in the replies, but one on one, it's in the DMs.
sentences.zh: 所以没错，这意味着你得去跟人说话，在社交媒体上，这发生在私信里或者回复里，但一对一的交流，是在私信里。

sentences.en: And for this to work for you, I would recommend prioritizing it.
sentences.zh: 为了让这件事对你有效，我建议你把它放在优先位置。

sentences.en: I would recommend time blocking it for 30 minutes on your calendar so that you actually sit down and do it right.
sentences.zh: 我建议你在日历上给它做时间块，每天 30 分钟，这样你才能真正坐下来把它做好。

sentences.en: 30 minutes on your calendar should be for researching validated posts and writing out ideas and actually drafting the posts.
sentences.zh: 日历上的 30 分钟应该用来研究经过验证的帖子、写下想法、实际起草帖子。

sentences.en: And then the other 30 minutes should be reaching out to people to get those posts shared right.
sentences.zh: 然后另外 30 分钟应该用来主动联系别人，让这些帖子被转发。

sentences.en: When you launch a product, that's practically what you're doing in the first place.
sentences.zh: 当你发布一个产品的时候，你一开始做的其实就是这件事。

sentences.en: To kick it off the ground is you're reaching out to people to see if they like the product and to see if they'll promote it, whether it's for money or not, or if they'll just use it.
sentences.zh: 把它推起来的方式，就是去联系别人，看他们喜不喜欢这个产品，看他们愿不愿意推广，不管付不付钱，或者他们愿不愿意直接用。

sentences.en: And if they do use it, boom. You have a user.
sentences.zh: 如果他们用了，砰，你就有了一个用户。

sentences.en: You think one user isn't a lot, but if you compound over time and then word of mouth kicks in, then you start growing organically.
sentences.zh: 你觉得一个用户不多，但如果你随着时间不断积累，然后口碑传播开始起作用，你就会开始自然增长。

sentences.en: The same thing works for building an audience.
sentences.zh: 同样的逻辑也适用于建立受众。

sentences.en: And so the goal here is to make actual friends, because what do friends do?
sentences.zh: 所以这里的目标是交真正的朋友，因为朋友会做什么？

sentences.en: They support each other and they're usually working toward the same goal.
sentences.zh: 他们互相支持，而且他们通常都在朝着同一个目标努力。

sentences.en: They have a similar value set.
sentences.zh: 他们有相似的价值观。

sentences.en: So if you have like five people that you're in communication with, and then you write or create a really good piece of content, and then you send it to them and you say, hey, I put a lot of time into this.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有大概五个人跟你在持续沟通，然后你写了一个或者创作了一个非常好的内容，你发给他们说，嘿，我在这上面花了很多时间。

sentences.en: I think you'll resonate with it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你会产生共鸣。

sentences.en: I think your audience will resonate with it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你的受众也会产生共鸣。

sentences.en: Can you share it now?
sentences.zh: 能帮我分享一下吗？

sentences.en: Obviously, it takes a bit of time to get to that point, which we're going to go over, but it really does become that simple once you actually have friends, because if they are friends, then they're more than happy to do that.
sentences.zh: 显然，要达到那个阶段需要一点时间，我们后面会讲，但一旦你真的有了朋友，事情就真的变得这么简单，因为如果他们是朋友，他们会很乐意帮你。

sentences.en: Like sharing something takes no effort, like it's not a big deal at all, but if the content sucks, then they're not going to want to do that.
sentences.zh: 分享东西又不费什么力气，根本不算什么大事，但如果内容很烂，他们就不会想帮你分享。

sentences.en: So go back to step one.
sentences.zh: 那就回到第一步。

sentences.en: So you know how to write good content and you're there to return the favor, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你知道怎么写好内容，而且你也会回报对方，对吧？

sentences.en: Like with Eden, when I go to my friends and I say, hey, I built this really cool thing, do you like it?
sentences.zh: 就像我跟 Eden，我去找我的朋友说，嘿，我做了个很酷的东西，你喜欢吗？

sentences.en: And they say, yes.
sentences.zh: 他们说喜欢。

sentences.en: And I say, okay, I'm launching this week. Will you help me promote it?
sentences.zh: 然后我说，好，我这周要发布，能帮我推广一下吗？

sentences.en: They'll say, sure.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，没问题。

sentences.en: And then like they have a lot of followers.
sentences.zh: 而且他们有很多粉丝。

sentences.en: So that's really helpful for me.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我帮助很大。

sentences.en: And so what I say, anytime that you launch product or any time you need something shared, please do not hesitate to send it to me so I can return the favor value exchange.
sentences.zh: 所以我会说，任何时候你要发布产品，或者需要分享什么东西，千万别犹豫，直接发给我，我也可以回报你，价值交换。

sentences.en: But if you don't have that friend group yet, I call this process.
sentences.zh: 但如果你还没有这样的朋友群，我把这个过程叫做——

sentences.en: Some of you may have heard of it non needy networking.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能听过——非乞讨式社交。

sentences.en: And so if you do this right, this is how you get someone like a 50,000 follower account to share your post.
sentences.zh: 如果你做对了，这就是你让一个五万粉丝的账号分享你内容的方法。

sentences.en: And now your post is in in front of 50,000 people and you didn't rely on the algorithm.
sentences.zh: 然后你的内容就会出现在五万人面前，而你完全没依赖算法。

sentences.en: And that's how you grow if you turn this into a repeatable process.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这个变成一个可重复的流程，这就是你增长的方式。

sentences.en: So the first step is to just find someone that you want to do.
sentences.zh: 第一步就是找到你想合作的人。

sentences.en: Obviously, like you shouldn't just reach out to anyone and everyone.
sentences.zh: 显然，你不应该随便找个人就联系。

sentences.en: This should be like a small, curated group of people that you're going to strategize and grow with over the course of 6 to 12 months, or probably even longer.
sentences.zh: 这应该是一个精心筛选的小群体，你会在未来六到十二个月，甚至更长的时间里，跟他们一起制定策略、共同成长。

sentences.en: Like, I have built so many long term friendships just by being on social media and being social.
sentences.zh: 我就是通过在社交媒体上活跃、主动社交，建立了太多长期的友谊。

sentences.en: I moved to Texas with JC Melina and Dakota Robertson like three years ago.
sentences.zh: 我三年前跟 JC Melina 和 Dakota Robertson 一起搬到了 Texas。

sentences.en: My buddy Joey lives down the street for me.
sentences.zh: 我哥们 Joey 就住在我这条街。

sentences.en: He literally moved here from Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 他真的是从 Atlanta 搬过来的。

sentences.en: My trainer Randy lives over there and we met online.
sentences.zh: 我的教练 Randy 也住在附近，我们是在网上认识的。

sentences.en: He was using my software, reached out.
sentences.zh: 他当时在用我的软件，然后联系了我。

sentences.en: He's like, hey, I know you like fitness and I know you do everything yourself, but let me do your meal plan and training.
sentences.zh: 他说，嘿，我知道你喜欢健身，也知道你什么事都自己来，但让我帮你做饮食计划和训练吧。

sentences.en: I think you'll like it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你会喜欢的。

sentences.en: I was like, fuck it, okay, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 我说，管他的，行，来吧。

sentences.en: And now we're very good friends and we're starting a new tropic business together.
sentences.zh: 现在我们是非常好的朋友，而且正在一起做一个新的 tropic 生意。

sentences.en: Like, it's it's so serendipitous how these things happen.
sentences.zh: 这些事情的发生真的太巧了。

sentences.en: And just opportunities pop up when you have people who either have opportunities or like the connection between you creates opportunities.
sentences.zh: 当你有了一群人，他们要么自己有机会，要么你们之间的联系会创造机会，机会就这么冒出来了。

sentences.en: I know that DMing other people is just like this non tangible strategy.
sentences.zh: 我知道去私信别人听起来像是一种摸不着的策略。

sentences.en: Like it just doesn't result in an immediate direct outcome as feedback, but I promise.
sentences.zh: 它不会立刻给你一个直接的反馈结果，但我向你保证。

sentences.en: If you do this like this is the greatest advantage you can have.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的去做，这会是你最大的优势。

sentences.en: And so where do you find these people that you want a DM on social media.
sentences.zh: 那你要私信的人去哪里找呢？就在社交媒体上找。

sentences.en: Like you kind of just take it easy, like you scroll if you see an account that you like, make an effort to dmn them.
sentences.zh: 你放轻松就行，刷动态的时候看到一个你喜欢的账号，就主动去私信他。

sentences.en: Make an effort to engage.
sentences.zh: 主动去互动。

sentences.en: Make an effort to be seen by them and to and for you to show that you're supportive.
sentences.zh: 主动让他们看到你，让他们知道你支持他们。

sentences.en: And if you just have time to look around like you can go to someone's profile that you like, like you can go to my profile and do this, I don't I don't know if it'll yield any results, but you just find people on social media by how you would find people on social media.
sentences.zh: 如果你有时间到处看看，你可以去你喜欢的某个人的主页，比如你可以去我的主页试试，我不确定会不会有什么结果，但你在社交媒体上找人，就用你在社交媒体上找人的方式就行。

sentences.en: There isn't like an exact way to just pinpoint exactly who to talk to.
sentences.zh: 没有一个精确的方法能直接锁定你该跟谁聊。

sentences.en: But you could go to like my profile, click on my following list who I'm following and see people who are similar to me or similar to you, and just go through them and see if you like any of their content.
sentences.zh: 但你可以去我的主页，点开我的关注列表，看看我关注了谁，找到那些跟我相似或者跟你相似的人，然后一个个翻，看看你喜不喜欢他们的内容。

sentences.en: And so step two, once you have someone that you want a DM, which should be pretty quick, you literally should just open social media, see someone, and then be like, that guy sounds cool, I'm going to.
sentences.zh: 第二步，一旦你找到了想私信的人——这应该很快，你基本上只需要打开社交媒体，看到一个人，然后觉得“这家伙挺酷的，我要去聊聊”。

sentences.en: But the second thing you do is you just send them simple praise, right?
sentences.zh: 第二步你要做的，就是给他们发一句简单的赞美。

sentences.en: Like, you don't have to do this.
sentences.zh: 你不一定要做这一步。

sentences.en: You can skip to further steps, but we're just getting into the flow of things here.
sentences.zh: 你可以跳到更后面的步骤，但我们先顺着这个节奏来。

sentences.en: You have to learn how to make friends. You just send simple praise.
sentences.zh: 你得学会怎么交朋友。你就发一句简单的赞美。

sentences.en: It's like how girls compliment each other's shoes or something like that, and then they're like, oh my God, girl, where do you get those?
sentences.zh: 就像女生互相夸对方的鞋子那样，然后她们就会说“天哪姐妹，你这在哪买的？”

sentences.en: And they start up a conversation and then one thing leads to another, and then they're getting lunch and then they're best friends.
sentences.zh: 然后她们就聊起来了，一件事接着一件事，然后她们就一起去吃午饭，然后就成了最好的朋友。

sentences.en: So what you do here is you go and look at the person's like content at their website, at what they're creating, if they're creating anything and you trying to find like something that you resonate with.
sentences.zh: 所以你要做的，就是去看看这个人的内容、他的网站、他在创作的东西——如果他有在创作的话——然后试着找到某个让你有共鸣的点。

sentences.en: And in my opinion, the simplest thing you can do here is to just send a single sentence.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，最简单的做法就是只发一句话。

sentences.en: So if someone wrote a social post that was like about how most people quit social media too early, I'd be like, damn, that's true.
sentences.zh: 比如有人发了一篇帖子，说大多数人放弃社交媒体太早了，我就会回一句：“靠，太真实了。”

sentences.en: I actually quit like four times and now I'm back at it.
sentences.zh: “我其实放弃了四次，现在又回来了。”

sentences.en: How long have you been a creator?
sentences.zh: “你当创作者多久了？”

sentences.en: Wow, so difficult to start a conversation.
sentences.zh: 哇，开启一段对话太难了。

sentences.en: You can ask GPT for how to start a conversation.
sentences.zh: 你可以问 GPT 怎么开启对话。

sentences.en: I wouldn't recommend it, but if you're that far gone socially, maybe try it.
sentences.zh: 我不推荐这么做，但如果你社交能力真的退化到那个地步了，也许可以试试。

sentences.en: The only other tip I can give with this step is to just avoid corporate speak like the plague, right?
sentences.zh: 这一步我能给的唯一其他建议就是：像躲瘟疫一样躲开那种职场套话。

sentences.en: You're not here to connect with someone on LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 你不是来 LinkedIn 上跟人建立商务联系的。

sentences.en: You're here to just, like, text them like a friend.
sentences.zh: 你就是来像朋友一样给他们发消息的。

sentences.en: Like you're just act as if you're passing by.
sentences.zh: 你就表现得像是路过一样。

sentences.en: You're at the gym, right?
sentences.zh: 你在健身房，对吧？

sentences.en: And you see someone with a similar shirt as you and you're like, oh, dude, nice shirt.
sentences.zh: 你看到一个人穿了件跟你很像的T恤，然后你说：“哦兄弟，T恤不错。”

sentences.en: And then that connection is kind of form.
sentences.zh: 然后那种连接就差不多形成了。

sentences.en: You go on about your workout and then you come back the next day, and then you see them again and you go, oh, what's up man?
sentences.zh: 你继续练你的，第二天再来，又看到他们，你说：“哟，怎么样兄弟？”

sentences.en: And you give them a fist bump and then you go home and you come back, and then you give them a fist bump again.
sentences.zh: 你跟他们碰个拳，然后回家，下次再来，再碰个拳。

sentences.en: You go, oh dude, I didn't get your name. What is it?
sentences.zh: 你走过去说，哦兄弟，我还不知道你叫什么，你叫什么名字？

sentences.en: And then you give her your name and they're like, oh, nice.
sentences.zh: 然后你告诉她你的名字，她说，哦，不错。

sentences.en: And then you just be like, oh, what's your what's your split?
sentences.zh: 然后你就随口问，哦，你今天练什么分化？

sentences.en: What are you training today?
sentences.zh: 你今天练什么？

sentences.en: And then they go, oh I'm training arms.
sentences.zh: 然后她说，哦我练手臂。

sentences.en: What about you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: And I'm like, yeah me too.
sentences.zh: 你就说，嗯我也一样。

sentences.en: And it's like, oh what are you training like on Saturday?
sentences.zh: 然后接着聊，哦那你周六练什么？

sentences.en: It's like chess. And they're like, oh, we should hit that together.
sentences.zh: 这就像下棋一样。然后她说，哦，我们可以一起练。

sentences.en: Do you come around this time?
sentences.zh: 你大概这个时间都会来吗？

sentences.en: And they'd be like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 她说，对。

sentences.en: And you'd be like, okay, cool, it's a date.
sentences.zh: 你就说，好，酷，就这么定了。

sentences.en: So it's literally the same exact thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这完全是一模一样的事情。

sentences.en: Like you're just doing it in the replies and the DM's as opposed to in the gym.
sentences.zh: 只不过你是在回复和私信里做这件事，而不是在健身房。

sentences.en: And rather than getting in a lift together, you support them in some way on sharing their content.
sentences.zh: 而且不是一起举铁，而是以某种方式支持他们分享内容。

sentences.en: And so that kind of covered step three, which is to just show interest in them.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就涵盖了第三步，就是对他们表现出兴趣。

sentences.en: So we are trying to do is drill into something that is important to them.
sentences.zh: 我们试图做的是深入挖掘对他们来说重要的事情。

sentences.en: And for another creator it's usually what they're building.
sentences.zh: 对另一个创作者来说，通常就是他们正在构建的东西。

sentences.en: Like you can ask them or what are you building?
sentences.zh: 你可以直接问他们，你在构建什么？

sentences.en: Or I see that you're building Eden, how is that going?
sentences.zh: 或者我看到你在做 Eden，进展怎么样？

sentences.en: What's the next feature you're going to drop?
sentences.zh: 下一个要发布的功能是什么？

sentences.en: I actually looked into it looks super cool.
sentences.zh: 我其实去了解了一下，看起来超酷。

sentences.en: I'm going to start using it or just be like, oh, I was on your Substack and I went back like a year ago, and you had this really good article that I read through in this part really resonated with me.
sentences.zh: 我准备开始用了。或者直接说，哦，我看了你的 Substack，我翻到了一年前的文章，你有一篇特别好的文章我仔细读完了，其中这一段让我特别有共鸣。

sentences.en: Like, where did you come up with that? Just something. Right?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么想到这个的？随便聊点什么，对吧？

sentences.en: It doesn't even matter. So step four is to show you are useful.
sentences.zh: 聊什么根本不重要。所以第四步是展示你是有用的。

sentences.en: And this is really where like the power comes into play, but it's also the part that trips people up the most because they don't think that they have any value to provide.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正力量发挥作用的地方，但也是卡住最多人的地方，因为他们不觉得自己有任何价值可以提供。

sentences.en: And the thing here is that, like you personally don't need any value to provide.
sentences.zh: 而关键在于，你个人不需要有任何价值可以提供。

sentences.en: Like you just need to be someone who can connect the other person with some form of value.
sentences.zh: 你只需要成为一个能把对方和某种价值连接起来的人。

sentences.en: That can be a resource, that can be a person.
sentences.zh: 可以是一个资源，可以是一个人。

sentences.en: If you need another person that you think that person should meet and just be like, dude, I think you should reach out to this guy.
sentences.zh: 如果你认识另一个人，你觉得对方应该认识，就直接说，兄弟，我觉得你应该联系一下这个人。

sentences.en: I think is really cool.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他真的很酷。

sentences.en: You guys would hit it off or what I really like doing, and what I really like when people do for me is when people know what I'm working on, or when I know what other people are working on, like me working on Eden.
sentences.zh: 你们俩肯定合得来。或者我个人很喜欢做、也很喜欢别人对我做的一件事是，当别人知道我在做什么，或者当我知道别人在做什么的时候，比如我在做 Eden。

sentences.en: Imagine I'm someone else.
sentences.zh: 假设我是另一个人。

sentences.en: If someone else were working on a software, then if I watch a YouTube video about AI and how it's going to disrupt tech and how this is the way forward,
sentences.zh: 如果另一个人也在做一款软件，然后我碰巧看了一个关于 AI 的 YouTube 视频，讲 AI 会如何颠覆科技、这就是未来的方向，

sentences.en: I would just send them the video and be like, hey, you might find this interesting.
sentences.zh: 我会直接把视频发给他们，说，嘿，你可能会觉得这个有意思。

sentences.en: I know you're building X, y, Z. Maybe this will impact it a bit and then they might watch it, or they'll just be like, thanks.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在做 X、Y、Z，说不定这个会有点影响，然后他们可能会看，或者就回一句谢谢。

sentences.en: Or they'll take mental note and be like, oh, that was really cool.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会在心里记下，觉得，哦，这挺酷的。

sentences.en: Like he thought of me outside of our DM's. And then that's when the law of reciprocity kicks in and they feel the need to return the favor.
sentences.zh: 他会觉得我在私信之外还想着他。这时候互惠法则就启动了，他们会觉得有必要回报这个人情。

sentences.en: If you give something, someone else is going to feel the need to give something in return.
sentences.zh: 你给了点什么，对方就会觉得需要回馈点什么。

sentences.en: So all you really need to do at that point is just ask, which we'll get to.
sentences.zh: 所以到这一步你真正需要做的，就是开口问，这个我们后面会讲。

sentences.en: But step five, which is an optional step, but highly recommended, is to just get on a call with the person.
sentences.zh: 但第五步，是可选的，但强烈推荐，就是直接跟对方打个电话。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: This is like getting coffee or getting lunch with someone you met at the gym or something of that nature, but online you kind of just be like, yo, we should catch up on a call sometime and talk about business.
sentences.zh: 这就好比你在健身房认识了谁，约着喝杯咖啡或吃个午饭，但在线上你大概就说，嘿，我们改天应该打个电话聊聊生意。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: And then you get on a call and then you come out of it with like a lot deeper connection.
sentences.zh: 然后你们通了电话，关系就会深很多。

sentences.en: The amount of calls that I got on when I was just beginning on social media was absurd.
sentences.zh: 我刚上社交媒体那会儿，打的电话数量多到离谱。

sentences.en: It's like people just like to speak with other people who have related interest, because they're not going to find those people in their everyday life, like there are very few people around me, or especially that I went to school with that have similar interests or that do similar things.
sentences.zh: 因为人们就是喜欢跟有共同兴趣的人聊天，他们在日常生活里找不到这样的人，我身边、尤其是我上学认识的人里，很少有相似兴趣或做类似事情的。

sentences.en: So you kind of have to build a tribe of those people so you can do that or you don't have to.
sentences.zh: 所以你得自己建一个这样的圈子，才能做到这一点，当然你不做也行。

sentences.en: But step number six is to just continue sending more resources or to just check in.
sentences.zh: 但第六步是，继续发更多资源，或者只是问候一下。

sentences.en: So you send them a video that you thought was interesting.
sentences.zh: 你发一个你觉得有意思的视频给他们。

sentences.en: You send them an article, you send them a tweet and be like, oh dude, this is exactly what we were talking about the other day.
sentences.zh: 你发一篇文章，发一条推文，说，兄弟，这完全就是我们前几天聊的那个。

sentences.en: You just kind of maintain faint connection while providing value to them.
sentences.zh: 你就是在保持一种轻度的联系，同时持续给他们提供价值。

sentences.en: Maybe you create something like, I've had many people scrape all my YouTube videos, which you don't have to do anymore because you can just go and eat in creators.
sentences.zh: 也许你创造点什么东西，比如，很多人把我所有 YouTube 视频都抓取下来了，现在你不用这么做了，因为你可以直接用 AI 去读创作者的内容。

sentences.en: Go to my YouTube chat with all the videos.
sentences.zh: 去我的 YouTube 频道，跟所有视频对话。

sentences.en: You don't have to spend thousands of dollars scraping with manis anymore to actually get the transcripts of people's YouTube videos.
sentences.zh: 你不用再花几千美元用 Manis 去抓取 YouTube 视频的转录文本了。

sentences.en: So try that out.
sentences.zh: 所以试试这个。

sentences.en: But they'll do that, and then they'll have the AI, like, get all of my stuff, like all of my patterns and all of my concepts in one place, and I'll be like, oh, that's really cool, and thank you for doing that.
sentences.zh: 但他们会这么做，然后让 AI 把我所有的东西、我所有的模式、我所有的概念都整合到一个地方，我就会觉得，哦，这真的很酷，谢谢你做了这个。

sentences.en: Even though I like that's what I do as like, you reverse engineer your own stuff.
sentences.zh: 尽管我自己就是这么做的，你逆向工程你自己的东西。

sentences.en: Like I have a database, not really a database, but I have a note of all of those things in one place already.
sentences.zh: 我有一个数据库，不完全是数据库，但我有一个笔记，已经把所有这些东西放在一个地方了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's good either way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不管怎样都挺好的。

sentences.en: But now step seven and finally.
sentences.zh: 但现在，第七步，也是最后一步。

sentences.en: And you don't need to go through all seven steps to do this.
sentences.zh: 你不需要走完所有七步才能做这件事。

sentences.en: It can just come naturally in the conversation.
sentences.zh: 它可以在对话中自然发生。

sentences.en: But this is where you ask and you can ask them a few things.
sentences.zh: 但这就是你开口问的时候了，你可以问他们几件事。

sentences.en: You can just ask them to join a group, chat with other people you've been talking to, and now you have this really powerful group chat where you can stir strategies, or you send them one of your posts that you put a lot of time into.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接邀请他们加入一个群组，跟你聊过的其他人一起聊天，这样你就有了一个非常强大的群聊，可以交流策略，或者你把一篇你花了大量时间写的帖子发给他们。

sentences.en: Or you can just ask them questions, right?
sentences.zh: 或者你直接问他们问题，对吧？

sentences.en: If they're an expert in a place that you're not, you have a connection where you can kind of get free answers out of them without paying for consulting or coaching.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在某个领域是专家而你不是，你就有了一个连接，可以免费从他们那里得到答案，不用付咨询费或教练费。

sentences.en: But if you plan to leverage their audience for growth, which isn't the goal of the friendship, but that's a benefit of it, you want to send them a post that you actually put a lot of time into, and that's good.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想借他们的受众来增长，这不是交朋友的目的，但这是附带的好处，你要发一篇你真的花了很多时间、而且质量很好的帖子给他们。

sentences.en: And then you ask them to share, because if it's not good, they're not going to want to share it.
sentences.zh: 然后你请他们分享，因为如果内容不够好，他们也不会想分享。

sentences.en: But this is also how you can come up with content ideas right?
sentences.zh: 但这也是你想出内容创意的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: In your conversation.
sentences.zh: 在你的对话里。

sentences.en: Something comes up like a problem or just some idea, and then you can write about that thing, and then you can send the post to them and be like, hey, I just wrote this up.
sentences.zh: 某个问题或者某个想法冒出来，然后你就可以写那个东西，再把帖子发给他们，说，嘿，我刚写了这个。

sentences.en: It was inspired by a previous conversation.
sentences.zh: 灵感来自我们之前的对话。

sentences.en: If you hit it with a share, I'll hit you back at some point.
sentences.zh: 如果你帮我分享一次，我之后也会帮你。

sentences.en: Or just be honest.
sentences.zh: 或者就坦诚一点。

sentences.en: Like my favorite outreach strategy in general is just brutal honesty and be like, hey dude, I'm really trying to grow.
sentences.zh: 我总体上最喜欢的 outreach 策略就是彻底的坦诚，直接说，嘿兄弟，我真的很想成长。

sentences.en: If you could share this, that would be awesome.
sentences.zh: 如果你能分享一下这个，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: If not, absolutely no worries at all.
sentences.zh: 如果不能，也完全没关系。

sentences.en: I'm not expecting anything.
sentences.zh: 我不期待任何回报。

sentences.en: And so that's literally it. You have two levers.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样。你有两个杠杆。

sentences.en: You can write validated content.
sentences.zh: 你可以写经过验证的内容。

sentences.en: And then if the algorithm doesn't magically pick it up, which it probably won't, especially if you're a beginner, then you have a manual way of making friends and having them share it to their audience so that it can at least get kickstarted.
sentences.zh: 如果算法没有奇迹般地把它推起来——大概率不会，尤其你还是新手——那你还有一条手动路径：交朋友，让他们把内容分享到自己的受众那里，这样至少能启动起来。

sentences.en: Is this all going to happen overnight? Is it going to happen tomorrow?
sentences.zh: 这一切会一夜之间发生吗？明天就会发生吗？

sentences.en: The next day?
sentences.zh: 后天？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 大概不会。

sentences.en: It's going to happen over the course of two weeks, four weeks, three months.
sentences.zh: 它会在两周、四周、三个月的过程里发生。

sentences.en: But it will compound and you'll definitely see some growth out of this, because these aren't levers that you guess at.
sentences.zh: 但它会复利增长，你一定会从中看到一些成长，因为这些杠杆不是靠猜的。

sentences.en: They're just levers that you pull.
sentences.zh: 它们就是你去拉动的杠杆。

sentences.en: It's just an action that you do and you get better at.
sentences.zh: 就是你去做、然后越做越好的一个动作。

sentences.en: It's a skill.
sentences.zh: 它是一项技能。

sentences.en: Not that you're going to DM 500 people, but if you DM'd five people a day for 30 days or 60 days, it's a lot of freaking people.
sentences.zh: 不是说你要给 500 个人发私信，但如果你每天给 5 个人发私信，坚持 30 天或 60 天，那人数就非常多了。

sentences.en: And if one isn't kind enough or close enough of a friend to share one of your posts, then you're doing something wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果其中没有一个人足够友善、或者跟你关系足够近、愿意分享你的一篇帖子，那你肯定哪里做错了。

sentences.en: So that's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: Those are the two ways to grow.
sentences.zh: 这就是增长的两种方式。

sentences.en: If you like this video, like the video, subscribe.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个视频，点赞，订阅。

sentences.en: If you want to research outlier content or have a place to write high performing content, check out the new version of Eden.
sentences.zh: 如果你想研究 outlier 内容，或者有一个地方来写高表现内容，去看看新版 Eden。

sentences.en: I think it's really cool because I like just saving links to boards and being able to write with them open next to it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它真的很酷，因为我喜欢把链接保存到看板上，然后能在旁边打开它们边看边写。

sentences.en: So check that out. I'm super excited about it.
sentences.zh: 去看看吧，我对这个特别兴奋。

sentences.en: Yeah. That's it. I'll see you in the next video. Bye.
sentences.zh: 好，就这样。下个视频见。拜。
